name: nexsift
description: nexsift is the filter for your homelab's notifications. Every service reports to nexsift instead of to your phone: Proxmox, Unraid, Uptime Kuma, Watchtower, Home Assistant, the NAS, the UPS. nexsift collects everything in one inbox, sorts it into info, warning and critical, bundles the routine into one line per source and passes on only what matters, through ntfy, Gotify, Telegram, Apprise, a webhook or straight to the phone as a Web Push notification. Senders need no plugin and no change, because nexsift answers like the services they already know: a Gotify server, an ntfy server, a Discord webhook, a mail server, a syslog server or a plain webhook. All-clears close problems instead of opening new lines, quiet hours and a storm guard keep the phone calm when many things fail at once, and rules decide level, bundling and push. One operator account with a password, optionally sign-in through several OpenID Connect providers side by side, Microsoft Entra ID among them (one-button setup for authentik), encrypted backups, a log without message content or tokens, read-only API keys for dashboards. The interface is available in English and German.

paths.name: Data (Container Path: /data)
paths.description: Holds the SQLite database with sources, rules, targets and messages, the key secret.key, backups and logs. Keep it on a local disk, not on a network share.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port you reach nexsift at. Also takes nexsift's own webhooks and Discord-style webhooks. Container port: 8000

ports.name: Gotify Port
ports.description: Answers like a Gotify server (POST /message), for Watchtower and everything else built on shoutrrr. Remove this port to close the door. Container port: 8001

ports.name: ntfy Port
ports.description: Answers like an ntfy server (POST /topic), including the subscription Home Assistant's ntfy integration opens. Remove this port to close the door. Container port: 8002

ports.name: SMTP Port
ports.description: Plain SMTP without sign-in, for a UPS, a printer or an old router that can only send mail. Map 25 here if a device cannot change its mail port. Remove this port to close the door. Container port: 2525

ports.name: Syslog Port (UDP)
ports.description: Syslog over UDP (RFC 3164 and 5424). Map 514 here if a device cannot change its syslog port and Unraid's own syslog server is off. Use the same number as the TCP port below. Container port: 5514

ports.name: Syslog Port (TCP)
ports.description: Syslog over TCP. Use the same number as the UDP port above. Container port: 5514

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User id that should own the files in /data. 99 is the Unraid default.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group id that should own the files in /data. 100 is the Unraid default.

variables.name: Time Zone
variables.description: The clock the quiet hours of push targets go by, for example Europe/Berlin. Leave blank for UTC.

variables.name: Ports as seen from outside
variables.description: The host ports above, for the setup hints on the sources page. Keep it in line whenever you change a port, or the hints send devices to the wrong number. Nothing else depends on it.

variables.name: Public URL
variables.description: The address people and senders use to reach nexsift, for example https://nexsift.example.com when it sits behind a reverse proxy. Used for the setup hints and the return address of OpenID Connect. Leave blank to take the address of the request; the setting under Settings wins when set.

variables.name: Trusted Proxies
variables.description: Addresses or networks of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto are believed, comma separated, for example 172.17.0.0/16. Only they can tell nexsift that a request came in over https. Leave blank when nexsift is not behind a proxy; blank trusts nobody, 127.0.0.1 included. A proxy on the same server with host networking: 127.0.0.1.

variables.name: Secret Key
variables.description: Protects the stored secrets: source tokens, push target credentials, the OpenID Connect client secret and the Web Push keys. Leave blank: nexsift creates one on first start and keeps it in /data/secret.key, and the backup archive carries it. When set, it wins over secret.key.

variables.name: Secure Cookie
variables.description: auto marks the session cookie Secure when the request arrived over https, also behind a proxy listed under Trusted Proxies that sends X-Forwarded-Proto. Use on only if a proxy terminates TLS and forwards plain http without that header, and never if nexsift should also be reachable over http, or nobody can sign in. off never marks it.
